source: Adapted from cinetic (https://github.com/Leonxlnx/cinetic, MIT, (c) 2026 Leonxlnx) — its measured technique library, rewritten for the medo-motion reel grammar (Pillow/canvas, vertical 1080x1920, Arabic type, no logo). Draw a film's moves with tools/techniques.py instead of reaching for the same four. The UI / product-demo / numbers / micro-interaction families were added for screen-based scenes: the recipes assume Medo's own art layer (`kit.phone`, `appWindow`, `checklist`, `rolling`, `art.laptop`, `follow_button`, `cursor`), not a recorded screen capture.

reel.what: A vertical 1080x1920 reel: Medo on paper, Arabic VO as the timing master, typographic end card, no logo and no series name.

techniques.name: Cold open mid-move
techniques.summary: No fade from black, no title card. Frame 1 is already in motion: the camera is mid-push, a word is half-built, the grid is already crawling. The first visible change lands inside 0.10 s.
techniques.how: Draw local time as t + 0.35 s into every entrance so nothing starts at rest: P `lib.prog(t+0.35,a,b)` / K `seg(t + 0.35, start, dur)`. Never call a fade at t=0; the paper flood, the pose and the HUD all exist on the first frame.
techniques.timing: first change ≤ 0.10 s; first readable word ≈ 0.40 s
techniques.use_when: Always. It is the cheapest way to read as directed instead of generated.
techniques.avoid_when: Never — the only exception is a deliberate cold open on a still, which must then slam within 0.4 s.

techniques.name: Question, then the first hard cut answers it
techniques.summary: The opening fragment is the question the viewer already has; the first hard cut (median 1.3 s in) lands the answer as a picture, not a caption.
techniques.how: Put the question as one 2–4 word fragment in scene 1, and make scene 1 end exactly where the VO's first silence starts (`plan/beats.json` bounds). The answer is the close-up pose (`presenter.draw(fr, 'close-explain', t)`) or the 3D object arriving on the cut, with the `sfx` hit on that frame — never another line of type.
techniques.timing: answer at 1.1–1.6 s, on the scene bound
techniques.use_when: A VO whose first sentence is a premise or a problem.
techniques.avoid_when: The VO opens with a personal greeting — then open on the pose instead.

techniques.name: The first word arrives with the move, not before it
techniques.summary: Nothing sits still waiting to be read. The first word enters at 40% ink and settles over 18–24 frames while the camera is still travelling.
techniques.how: P: `paste(sp, y+rise*(1-e_out(p)), alpha=0.4+0.6*e_out(p))` with rise 25 px over 0.6 s; K: `enter(t, start, {dur:0.62, from:0.4, rise:25})`. The camera keeps creeping (`cam-living-hold-creep`) underneath.
techniques.timing: 18–24 f settle at 30 fps, 4–10 f between words
techniques.use_when: Every title, every fragment.
techniques.avoid_when: Never pair it with a scale start above 1.17× — that reads as a zoom, not a settle.

techniques.name: One beat of still, then the slam
techniques.summary: A single deliberate empty beat (≤0.5 s in this studio) buys the first slam its weight. Used once per film, on the key claim.
techniques.how: Hold the pose and the paper still for 12–15 f, keep breathing only (`presenter.breathe`), then land the word at 1.4–2.1× scale with 2–4 f of `blur_steps` smear and settle in 20 f.
techniques.timing: still 0.4–0.5 s, slam settles over 0.7 s
techniques.use_when: Once, on the line the film is actually about.
techniques.avoid_when: Twice in one reel, or anywhere the VO is still talking over it.

techniques.name: Masked baseline rise
techniques.summary: Each word rises out of its own clipped line box, darkening from grey to ink. Whole words only — the mask is per word, never per letter.
techniques.how: P: build a sprite per word with `lib.text_sprite`, paste through a clip box whose height grows with `e_out(p)`; colour lerps `gray_4 → ink` over the same p. K: `ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.rect(x, lineTop, w, lineH*e); ctx.clip(); drawWord(...)`. Words 8 f apart, 10–12 f each.
techniques.timing: 10–12 f per word, 8 f apart (30 fps)
techniques.use_when: The default entrance for Arabic headlines — it respects shaping because the clip never cuts a letter.
techniques.avoid_when: On a word that must be readable in under 0.4 s (a hook word) — use the settle instead.

techniques.name: In-place light-up on the beat
techniques.summary: The finished line is laid out first; words light from `gray_2` to ink on successive grid steps, so the type follows the tempo without moving.
techniques.how: Lay the whole line at final positions, then per word pick a step from `beat.grid(bpm)` (`on_grid`) and ramp colour over 4 f. The newest word may take `red` for 12–24 f then settle to ink — once per card, not per word.
techniques.timing: 1 step per word at 100–120 BPM, ramp 4 f, recency 12–24 f
techniques.use_when: Long Arabic lines where motion would fight readability.
techniques.avoid_when: More than 8 words visible — the line becomes a scan.

techniques.name: Re-centring line build
techniques.summary: Words arrive right-to-left (Arabic reading order) and the line re-centres once per word on an expo-out, never per letter.
techniques.how: Compute the final line width once; after each word lands, tween the line origin to `0.5 - width/2` with `e_out` over 24–38 f. Keep the vertical baseline fixed so only x breathes.
techniques.timing: 24–38 f re-centre, words 6–9 f apart
techniques.use_when: A short claim that grows to most of the frame width.
techniques.avoid_when: RTL is on and the words contain punctuation-only tokens — group them with the previous word first.

techniques.name: Staggered word roll
techniques.summary: The outgoing word rises and blurs out while the incoming word comes up from below — a vertical roller inside one line, 5–6 f per word.
techniques.how: Two sprites per slot: outgoing at `y - 20*e`, `blur_steps` 6 px, alpha out over 10 f; incoming from `y + 24` settling in 20 f. Drive the slot changes from `beat` steps so it never drifts.
techniques.timing: 5–6 f per word, 20 f settle
techniques.use_when: A list of three to five short Arabic terms that share a grammar.
techniques.avoid_when: Words longer than ~10 characters — the roll outruns the eye.

techniques.name: Reading-order exit
techniques.summary: Text rarely fades on its own. It leaves on the cut, or word by word in reading order, each rising 10–20 px and gone in 2–3 f.
techniques.how: Trigger the exit 6–8 f before the scene bound from `plan/beats.json`, front to back (Arabic: right to left), with the background already accelerating out (`transition` velocity curve).
techniques.timing: exit finished 2 f before the cut
techniques.use_when: Every fragment that does not die with its whole scene.
techniques.avoid_when: A hero line — it goes with the cut instead, never a slow fade.

techniques.name: Oversize word with velocity blur
techniques.summary: One word at 15–30% of frame height travels in fast with directional blur, then goes pin-sharp within 10 f and is legible by 0.5 s.
techniques.how: Speed from the timeline (`velocity`), smear with `blur_steps(vx, vy)` (P) / `drawBlurred` (K), then draw the crisp pass once the speed drops under ~12 px/f. Blur lives only on the fast frames.
techniques.timing: sharp within 0.33 s, readable by 0.5 s
techniques.use_when: A two-word punchline in the middle act.
techniques.avoid_when: On a word the VO is also saying slowly — the two rhythms fight.

techniques.name: Title behind Medo, then reveal
techniques.summary: A short, oversized Arabic title sits behind Medo’s transparent pose. At a VO-aligned hard cut, omit the pose but keep the same title layer, size and baseline; the cutout has been masking the title, and the cut reveals the full phrase without reflow or a duplicate title.
techniques.how: P: create one shaped title sprite with `lib.text_sprite`, paste it first, then draw the alpha pose with `presenter.draw(fr, pose, t)` above it. K: draw the full title with `arabic.setArabic` + `fillText` first, then `presenter.drawPresenter(ctx, pose, t)`; at the cut stop drawing the pose and keep the title coordinates/font unchanged. Use existing Medo pose PNG alpha only; keep the phrase short, RTL-shaped and out of the caption-safe band. Check face/text overlap and frames immediately before/on/after the cut. This is a P/K recipe; do not assume an R port.
techniques.timing: short punch settles before the VO-aligned cut; title holds unchanged for ≥0.5 s after the pose exits
techniques.use_when: One verified, high-value 1–3-word claim can be set behind a Medo pose and then read clearly on its own.
techniques.avoid_when: Long copy, dense diagrams, subtitles, or when the title crosses the face/important pose details; skip if the Arabic shaping or final hold is not clean.

techniques.name: Scaled echo extrusion
techniques.summary: A word is repeated behind itself at stepped scales and descending opacity, reading as depth without a gradient or a glow.
techniques.how: Draw the sprite 4–7 times at `scale = 1 + i*0.06`, alpha `0.30 * (1 - i/n)`, offset 2–4 px per step, in `ink_shadow`; the front copy is full ink. Cheap, flat, and on-palette.
techniques.timing: static, revealed with the word (0.4 s)
techniques.use_when: The one word that should feel monumental.
techniques.avoid_when: Small type, or over a textured background — the echoes turn to mush.

techniques.name: Vertical word stack
techniques.summary: Words stack down the 9:16 frame like a column, one per line, each landing on its own step — it turns the vertical format into an advantage.
techniques.how: One word per line at 12–16% of frame height, line pitch 1.15×, each arriving 6–8 f after the last on `e_out`, stacked from the top safe line downward; measure every word with `lib.text_sprite` first so a long word cannot overflow the 40 px margin, and give the last line the accent.
techniques.timing: 6–8 f per line at 100 BPM
techniques.use_when: Three to five short terms, or a list that must fill the tall frame.
techniques.avoid_when: Words longer than the frame width at that size — check with the measured sprite width first.

techniques.name: Scramble decode (Latin readouts only)
techniques.summary: A mono readout resolves from random glyphs, one character at a time. It is a Latin/mono device: Arabic is banned from it.
techniques.how: For HUD numbers and mono labels only (`IBM Plex Mono`), seed a `rng(seed)` and reveal left to right in 12–18 f. Arabic never uses it — per-letter reveal breaks shaping and the studio rules.
techniques.timing: 12–18 f, always shorter than the word it decorates
techniques.use_when: A counter, a timestamp, a version tag.
techniques.avoid_when: Any Arabic word, any word the viewer must read.

techniques.name: Velocity handoff cut
techniques.summary: The outgoing shot accelerates over its last 0.3–0.6 s and the next shot starts at exactly that speed, so the cut is felt as one move.
techniques.how: Before a bound: ease in to the exit (`x = e_in(p)`), peak 25–45 px/f at 1080-wide, and start the next scene with the same velocity decaying (`*0.92` per frame, τ ≈ 12 f at 30 fps). Keep the camera vector identical across the cut.
techniques.timing: exit accel 10–18 f, decay τ ≈ 12 f
techniques.use_when: The default cut — it is the highest-evidence move in the library.
techniques.avoid_when: Between two static cards; with no speed to hand over it just looks like a jolt.

techniques.name: Scale-through cut
techniques.summary: A shape (a word, a pill, the pose's silhouette) grows past the frame, and the next shot is revealed inside the same shape at the same scale rate.
techniques.how: Animate a mask rect/rounded-rect from 0.2× to 3× with `e_in` over 14–18 f, swap the plate at the peak, then continue outward from 3× to rest. `transition.layer()` masks already support this.
techniques.timing: 14–18 f each way at 30 fps
techniques.use_when: Act changes, or when a word becomes a container.
techniques.avoid_when: Twice in a row — it reads as a template.

techniques.name: Polarity flip cut
techniques.summary: Paper becomes ink (or the reverse) on the frame of the cut, with type and pose re-coloured instantly. No dissolve, no fade.
techniques.how: Flip the `THEME` flag on the cut frame and swap the two role colours (`paper ↔ ink`, `ink_shadow ↔ gray_1`); the pose sprite is re-tinted by its alpha mask, and the SFX hit lands on the same frame. It is a hard cut that changes world.
techniques.timing: instant, on the scene bound
techniques.use_when: Acts that must feel like chapters.
techniques.avoid_when: More than twice — the film starts to strobe.

techniques.name: Shape match cut
techniques.summary: Something in shot A (a circle, a bar, the mouth of a cup) is in the same place, size and colour as something in shot B, so the eye carries the object across.
techniques.how: Choose the match object once per film (the dot, the bar, the ring) and reuse it as the carrier — `lc-one-centred-subject` and `tr-dot-relay` both depend on it. Match centre within 6 px and radius within 4%.
techniques.timing: the match holds for 2–4 f around the cut
techniques.use_when: When the film has a story device (it should).
techniques.avoid_when: Two diagonal compositions — the eye has no anchor to match.

techniques.name: Dot relay into the next scene
techniques.summary: Everything collapses to one dot, the dot travels, and the next scene grows out of it. The device the film owns is the thing that survives the cut.
techniques.how: Fade the composition to the accent dot over 8–10 f (`e_in`), carry the dot along a 40–70 px/f path across the cut, then scale the next scene from 0.05× around the dot in 12–16 f.
techniques.timing: 10 f collapse, 12–16 f growth
techniques.use_when: Mid-film, to link two unrelated pictures.
techniques.avoid_when: Collapsing to a dot that then means nothing — the relay must be the same object.

techniques.name: Reveal by subtraction
techniques.summary: The frame is over-full, then everything that is not the point is removed in one move, leaving one object, one word, one pose.
techniques.how: Start with 3–5 layered props (`lc-one-centred-subject` inverse), then run a single scale-and-delete pass over 18–24 f in one direction, keeping the hero element exactly in place.
techniques.timing: 18–24 f, one direction only
techniques.use_when: The moment the film makes its single point.
techniques.avoid_when: As a habit — it costs a whole scene to earn.

techniques.name: Living hold creep
techniques.summary: Nothing is ever locked. A held shot creeps 1.5–3 px/f with one direction change, so the frame is alive while the eye reads.
techniques.how: `z = 1 + 0.02*e_io(p)` plus `tx = 6*sin(2πt/T)` with T = 6–9 s, under any readable text. Cap the speed at 3 px/f — faster and the type stops being sharp.
techniques.timing: continuous, one direction change per 6–9 s
techniques.use_when: Every shot longer than 1 s.
techniques.avoid_when: Nowhere — a locked camera is the tell that the sheet is generated.

techniques.name: Punch-in insert
techniques.summary: At the cut, the same plate punches in 1.25–1.6× and lands a beat later — the cheapest way to make one scene feel like two.
techniques.how: Because Medo ships `full` and `bust` framings of the same pose (`assets/poses/poses.json`), cut from `explain` to `close-explain` and add 1.15–1.3× scale over 6 f so the face lands at the same size. Pure crop, no new art.
techniques.timing: 6–8 f punch, settle 12 f
techniques.use_when: Emphasis on a single sentence, inside one VO scene.
techniques.avoid_when: More than once per scene — it stops meaning 'listen'.

techniques.name: Isolating push
techniques.summary: A slow push toward the one object that matters while the rest of the frame drifts out of the safe area.
techniques.how: `z: 1 → 1.18` over 20–30 f with `e_io`, target = the object's centre, plus a matched push on the type layer at half the amount so the parallax reads as depth.
techniques.timing: 0.7–1.0 s push
techniques.use_when: Before a reveal or a number.
techniques.avoid_when: When the push would move the caption out of the safe margin.

techniques.name: Layered parallax truck
techniques.summary: Background, pose and type move at different rates. The depth comes from speed, not from blur or shadow.
techniques.how: Offset each layer by `k` px/f with k = 0.35 / 1.0 / 1.8 for bg / presenter / type, each layer padded 8% so nothing pops at the edges. Works in both engines with a translate.
techniques.timing: continuous, 0.8–1.5 px/f
techniques.use_when: A quiet explanation beat that still has to breathe.
techniques.avoid_when: Over a busy paper texture — the layers stop separating.

techniques.name: Pull-back that lands an event
techniques.summary: The camera pulls out and the thing it reveals lands exactly on the last frame of the move — the move causes the event.
techniques.how: `z: 1.4 → 1.0` with `e_out` over 18 f, and put the word/object arrival on the final 2 f, with the SFX on that frame.
techniques.timing: 18 f pull, event on the last 2 f
techniques.use_when: An end-of-sentence payoff.
techniques.avoid_when: If the reveal is larger than the frame — it will pop.

techniques.name: Crane down with a delayed push
techniques.summary: A vertical crane (the format's own axis) with the push starting 6–8 f later, so two moves read as one gesture.
techniques.how: `ty: +40 → 0` on `e_io` over 24 f; the push `z: 1 → 1.1` starts 8 f in on the same curve family. In 9:16 the vertical axis is the one with the most room, so this is the house crane.
techniques.timing: 24 f crane, push offset 8 f
techniques.use_when: Scene openings between two VO sentences.
techniques.avoid_when: Two cranes back to back.

techniques.name: Hero push with a 3D turn
techniques.summary: The camera pushes while the object turns — the one move that makes the 3D layer worth having.
techniques.how: `space3d.camera(dist, yaw, pitch)` with yaw sweeping −35° → +35° over 30–40 f while `dist` drops 12%; keep `sorted_faces` + `shade` on, back-face cull on `dot(n, cam.pos − face_centre) ≤ 0`.
techniques.use_when: The single 3D hero moment of the reel.
techniques.avoid_when: Yaw beyond ±80° (the cull breaks) or more than one per film.

techniques.name: Object on a thick extruded slab
techniques.summary: A flat thing (a card, a word plate) gets real thickness and a slow orbit, so it casts its own edge shadow in-palette.
techniques.how: `space3d.prism(poly2d, depth)` with depth 6–10% of width, cap role `paper`, side role `gray_2`, plus a 2 px hairline in `ink` on the front cap and the floor shadow as a squashed `ink_shadow` ellipse.
techniques.use_when: Turning a flat prop into the film's object.
techniques.avoid_when: Depth above 12% — it reads as a crate.

techniques.name: Edge-on sliver snaps face-on
techniques.summary: The object starts as a 1-pixel-thin sliver seen edge-on, then rotates to face the camera in 10 f — a reveal with no fade anywhere.
techniques.how: `yaw = 90° → 8°` with front-loaded easing (35% of the rotation in the first frame, blurred: `blur_steps`), `shade` ramping as the normal turns toward the light.
techniques.timing: 10 f to face-on, 20 f settle
techniques.use_when: Revealing the key word-plate or the closing statement.
techniques.avoid_when: Twice in one act.

techniques.name: 3D flip that swaps the state
techniques.summary: A 180° flip hides the swap: the back face is already the new word/picture when it lands.
techniques.how: Rotate the plate about y with `space3d`, cull the back face, and swap the texture at 90°; 2–3 f of `blur_steps` at the fastest frame. The flip is 10 f and never bounces.
techniques.timing: 10 f flip, no overshoot
techniques.use_when: A before/after pair, or two opposite words.
techniques.avoid_when: Any overshoot or spring on the landing.

techniques.name: Tilted object on a spotlit ground
techniques.summary: The ground is a pool of light and everything else is darkness; the object sits tilted inside it, lit from one side.
techniques.how: `shade(color, normal, light=[0.35,0.75,0.55])` with ambient 0.45 gives the ramp with zero gradient code; the pool is a hard-edged `paper` ellipse under the object, and the rest of the stage is `ink`.
techniques.timing: static hold with the camera creep
techniques.use_when: A quiet beat that still needs weight.
techniques.avoid_when: Over the light theme — the pool has nothing to contrast against.

techniques.name: Caption in the subject's negative space
techniques.summary: The caption lives in the part of the frame the pose leaves empty, so the presenter and the type never fight.
techniques.how: `presenter.draw(..., x=0.62)` puts the pose right; the caption block sits left of its bounding box at 58 px Cairo, on the 40 px margin. Mirror it (x=0.38) on the next scene to keep the frame from settling into one template.
techniques.timing: as long as the VO phrase
techniques.use_when: Every sentence that runs while Medo is on screen.
techniques.avoid_when: The pose is centred and large — then use `lc-one-centred-subject` instead.

techniques.name: One huge centred subject
techniques.summary: Exactly one thing in the middle of the frame, at 40–70% of its height, with everything else empty paper.
techniques.how: Choose the object or the pose, place it on the optical centre (y ≈ 0.46 H, not the geometric centre), and delete every other element. The caption, if any, goes above or below on the margin, never both.
techniques.timing: one scene
techniques.use_when: The claim, the number, the turn.
techniques.avoid_when: Two scenes in a row — the film stops moving.

techniques.name: Words part for an inserted object
techniques.summary: A line of type splits at its centre word, the object rises through the gap, and the line closes again — the insertion is the transition.
techniques.how: Measure the line, split it into two sprites, offset them apart by `gap = 0.25 * wordWidth * e_io(p)` over 12 f, run the object through on the vertical axis, close over 12 f.
techniques.timing: 12 f open, 14 f insert, 12 f close
techniques.use_when: A demonstration that needs to interrupt a sentence.
techniques.avoid_when: A line wider than the safe area once split.

techniques.name: Phrase chunks on the grid
techniques.summary: Every picture event lands on a grid step, and the VO's phrases are cut into chunks that map onto bars — so the edit and the tempo are the same object.
techniques.how: `beat.grid(bpm)` gives the steps; `vo_length.py --bpm` snaps the scene bounds onto them first, then place events at `on_grid(bpm, bar, step)`. A cut that drifts 110 ms off the grid reads as layered, not composed.
techniques.timing: hero events within ±1 f of a step; everything within ±40 ms
techniques.use_when: Always — this is the spine the other moves hang from.
techniques.avoid_when: Never; if the VO has no tempo, pick 100 BPM and snap within 0.12 s.

techniques.name: Breath envelope per card
techniques.summary: Each card opens on a burst, decays into a reading plateau, and hands its energy to the next card — a sawtooth, not a flat line.
techniques.how: Per scene: the first 20–25% of the frames carry the entrance (`prog` on an `e_out` curve), the rest is a cruise at 1.5–3 px/f, and the last 8–10 f accelerate into the cut. Take the scene's own bounds from `plan/beats.json`, and its length in beats from `beat.bar_seconds`.
techniques.timing: burst 0.3–0.5 s, plateau 1–3 s, exit 0.27 s
techniques.use_when: Every scene longer than 1.2 s.
techniques.avoid_when: Very short punctuation scenes — they are all burst.

techniques.name: Light and dark as chapters
techniques.summary: The reel's acts are separated by the stage's luminance, not by a label: paper act, ink act, paper act. It gives structure with zero on-screen furniture.
techniques.how: Assign `THEME` per act from the VO's own structure (question, proof, close). The light act is `drawPaper` with `paperTile`, the dark one the paper inverse; flip on a scene bound with `tr-polarity-flip-cut` and keep the accent's meaning constant across the flip.
techniques.timing: per act (2–4 per reel)
techniques.use_when: Reels longer than ~25 s.
techniques.avoid_when: Alternating every scene — that is a strobe, not a structure.

techniques.name: Machine on the grid, hands off it
techniques.summary: The geometric layer is rigidly quantised; the presenter and the hand-made props are deliberately not. The contrast is the personality.
techniques.how: Grid, HUD and type land on `beat` steps to the frame; the pose bobs/sways on `presenter.bob` and `presenter.sway` with a phase offset, and the paper texture is fixed to the world, not to the beat.
techniques.timing: grid ±0 f, human layer ±80 ms
techniques.use_when: Any reel where Medo is on screen — that is all of them.
techniques.avoid_when: Nothing. Do not quantise the presenter.

techniques.name: Silence as the default bed
techniques.summary: There is no music under the voice. The soundtrack is the VO plus hits that are caused by something on screen — and one deliberate hole before the biggest moment.
techniques.how: `sfx.py` events are keyed to picture events (a cut, a landing, a flip), never to a bar counter alone. Before the key claim, drop the sub for 12–15 f and release it on the cut. Target −14.5 ± 0.3 LUFS integrated, TP ≤ −1.5 dBTP after the mux.
techniques.timing: hole 12–15 f before the hero cut
techniques.use_when: Always — the voice is the score.
techniques.avoid_when: Medo explicitly asks for a music bed.

techniques.name: Every hit is caused by something you can see
techniques.summary: An SFX fires only on the frame where a visible thing lands. No ambient ticking, no filler whooshes, no sound for a cut nobody sees.
techniques.how: Drive `sfx.py` from the same event list the picture uses (`grid_cues` / the scene's event table), with the cue on the exact frame of the landing. One sound per event, and the kit is synthesized (`tools/sfx_kit.py`).
techniques.timing: cue frame = landing frame (±0 f)
techniques.use_when: Every sound in the reel.
techniques.avoid_when: Never — an unattributed sound is the audio version of filler text.

techniques.name: Speed-gated motion blur
techniques.summary: Blur appears only above ~20–40 px/f and only on the fast frames; everything settled is pin-sharp. It is physics, not a filter.
techniques.how: `velocity(t)` → if `speed > 20`: `blur_steps(vx, vy, n=6)` (P) or `drawBlurred` (K) with 6–16 px of smear; below that draw crisp. Never blur a whole scene or a still.
techniques.timing: per frame, from the real velocity
techniques.use_when: Slams, whips, flips, scale-throughs.
techniques.avoid_when: Slow type or a delivered still — blur there reads as a cheap filter.

techniques.name: Paper grain and hairline edges
techniques.summary: The texture that sells the material: frame-keyed paper grain, hairlines on the objects, and one key shadow — no vignette bloom, no gradient overlays.
techniques.how: K: `paperTile(seed)` + `drawPaper`; P: the existing `make_bg` grid + grain. Hairline = 2 px `ink` at 20–35% alpha, shadow = `ink_shadow` at 18% offset 14 px with a 36 px blur, both from `kit.withShadow`.
techniques.timing: static texture, rebuilt per frame with a frame-keyed seed
techniques.use_when: Always, both engines — it is what makes the palette look printed.
techniques.avoid_when: Never animate the grain; a crawling texture reads as noise.

techniques.name: The state changes on the tap frame
techniques.summary: A screen is only worth its runtime if it changes. The tap lands, the ring blooms for four frames, and the state swaps on that exact frame — never a crossfade between two states.
techniques.how: K: draw the screen inside `phone(ctx, x, y, w, drawScreen)` or `card(...)`, and switch the branch of `drawScreen` on the tap frame (t >= tap); the touch ring is a `circle_spr`-style disc at the touch point for 4-6 f with the `sfx` hit on that frame. P: `art.follow_button(pressed=True)` then `done=True` — two cached sprites, one swap.
techniques.timing: ring 4-6 f, swap instant, settle 8 f
techniques.use_when: Any beat where Medo says 'and then it…' — the picture finishes his sentence.
techniques.avoid_when: Two state swaps inside one caption; the eye reads change, not menus.

techniques.name: A row slides in and the list makes room
techniques.summary: Instead of dropping a row on top, the new row arrives from below while the rows under it shift by exactly one pitch — the room-making is the motion.
techniques.how: Keep the list as data (y, text); on insert animate every y with `e_out` over 10-12 f and give the new row the same `enter()` curve from below. Draw rows with `kit.card` (K) or `fill_rect` + `lib.text_sprite` (P). Never fade the old rows out.
techniques.timing: 10-12 f shift, new row lands 2 f later
techniques.use_when: Lists, results, messages, checklists that grow.
techniques.avoid_when: More than five visible rows on 9:16 — the pitch drops under the 27 px readable floor.

techniques.name: Checklist ticks on the grid
techniques.summary: A checklist ticks one item per grid step, each tick drawing itself in eight frames — the tempo does the counting.
techniques.how: K: `checklist(ctx, items, t, {start, step})` with step = one beat. P: pre-render `paper_spec(checks=n)` variants and paste the one whose n matches the step, plus the `checkmark(s)` sprite for the tick. Take the steps from `beat.grid(bpm)` so a cut never lands mid-tick.
techniques.timing: 1 item per beat, 8-10 f per tick
techniques.use_when: Proving a process while the voice-over counts along.
techniques.avoid_when: Items that cannot be read in one beat (over five words).

techniques.name: A sheet rises over a dimmed screen
techniques.summary: A bottom sheet slides up over the screen and the screen behind drops to 60% — the depth cue is the dim, never a glow or a blur.
techniques.how: Draw the screen first, then an ink overlay at 0.35 alpha, then `kit.card` from below the frame to its rest position with `e_out` over 12-14 f (`around` handles the translate). Scale the background to 0.92 so the sheet reads as closer.
techniques.timing: 12-14 f up, 6 f settle
techniques.use_when: A detail the wide screen cannot show, or the closing call.
techniques.avoid_when: A sheet over a sheet; two is a stack nobody reads.

techniques.name: The focus ring travels, and snaps
techniques.summary: The active outline jumps between options in eight frames and the colour flips at mid-travel instead of tweening — a decision, not a gradient.
techniques.how: Two fixed ring positions from the layout; interpolate `e_io` over 8 f, and switch the stroke from `gray_1` to `red` at p = 0.5 (`rr()` + strokeStyle in K, `rrect(..., outline=...)` in P). The colour is chosen by p, never interpolated.
techniques.timing: 8 f travel, colour flip at 4 f
techniques.use_when: Choosing between two or three options on a screen.
techniques.avoid_when: Long menus or lists — the ring reads as flicker.

techniques.name: Phone in Medo's hand
techniques.summary: The prop is attached to the presenter, not floating: the phone inherits the pose's bob and sway and its screen runs its own animation inside.
techniques.how: Draw `presenter.draw(fr, 'phone', t)` (or 'seated-talk') and place the device at the pose's hand anchor; apply the same `presenter.bob(t)` and `presenter.sway(t)` offsets to the device, never an independent float. K: `poseFrame(...)` then `phone(ctx, ...)` with those two offsets added.
techniques.timing: as long as the scene
techniques.use_when: Any beat where the product lives on a phone — the default for this studio.
techniques.avoid_when: A full-body pose whose hand is out of frame; check the anchor before committing.

techniques.name: The cursor does the demo
techniques.summary: The viewer watches a hand: the cursor travels at reading speed, presses, and the interface answers. One action per sentence.
techniques.how: `art.cursor(s)` in P, the same path in K: travel 30-60 px/f, `blur_steps` above 20 px/f, a 3 f press dip, then the state change via `ui-state-change-on-tap`. One cursor only, and it never leaves the 40 px safe margin.
techniques.timing: travel 12-20 f, press 3 f
techniques.use_when: Explaining a flow that lives on a screen.
techniques.avoid_when: Two cursors, or a cursor moving while the VO talks about something else.

techniques.name: The window builds itself
techniques.summary: Frame, then content, then result: the window assembles in three steps on consecutive beats instead of appearing finished.
techniques.how: K: `appWindow(ctx, x, y, w, h, {title, body})` and reveal the body progressively (rows after 8 f, result after 16 f). P: `art.laptop()` or `art.desktop()` as the frame, with `fill_rect` rows over it. One accent for the result only.
techniques.timing: 3 steps x 8-10 f inside one 1.2 s scene
techniques.use_when: Introducing a tool or a screen for the first time.
techniques.avoid_when: Rebuilding the same window later in the reel — reuse the render.

techniques.name: Before and after, cut not faded
techniques.summary: The same screen in two states, swapped on a hard cut with the layout identical — the eye can compare because nothing else moves.
techniques.how: Render the same layout twice — the same `card(...)` / `phone(ctx, ...)` body with different data — and cut on the grid, keeping every element's position fixed so only the values change. One element may move: then use `d3-flip-face-swap` instead of a dissolve.
techniques.timing: cut on the grid, no blend
techniques.use_when: Proving a change with one variable.
techniques.avoid_when: Both states cluttered — the comparison dies.

techniques.name: The counter rolls and lands on the beat
techniques.summary: A number rolls from its old value to its new one and locks two frames before the step — the number is part of the tempo.
techniques.how: K: `rolling(from, to, p, {digits})` with p from `prog(t, start, start + dur)`. P: draw the digits from the same easing (`e_out`), one sprite per value band. Arabic digits when the VO says the number in Arabic, Latin mono when the voice says it in English.
techniques.timing: 8-14 f roll, lock 2 f before the step
techniques.use_when: Every number whose value the voice-over states.
techniques.avoid_when: Values that are not in the script — a fake metric is filler.

techniques.name: The bar grows, then the label lands
techniques.summary: The bar reaches its value first and the number arrives eight frames later — two arrivals read as causality, one arrival reads as a slide.
techniques.how: `fill_rect` (P) or `rr` + fill (K) from 0 to the value with `e_out` over 14-18 f; the track is `gray_1`, the bar `red`, no gradient; then draw the label with the settle from `oh-word-arrives-with-the-move`.
techniques.timing: 14-18 f bar, label +8 f
techniques.use_when: Comparisons, progress, growth.
techniques.avoid_when: More than three bars; the frame becomes a chart nobody asked for.

techniques.name: One number, full bleed
techniques.summary: A single number at 30-40% of the frame height with everything else deleted — if the reel has one memorable figure, this is where it is spent.
techniques.how: One `lib.font(size, 'Anton', 900)` sprite (Cairo 900 for Arabic digits), optical centre at y around 0.46 H, no outline and no glow; the unit is a small `IBM Plex Mono` line eight frames later. Once per reel.
techniques.timing: 0.8-1.5 s on screen
techniques.use_when: The one figure the film exists to say.
techniques.avoid_when: A second time, or a decimal nobody needs.

techniques.name: The unit arrives after the digits
techniques.summary: EGP, %, /day comes in six to eight frames after the digits settle, at 30% opacity, and tightens into place.
techniques.how: Separate sprite, `enter()` with from 0.3, rise 8 px, starting 6-8 f after the number settles. In Arabic keep the unit as its own word (RTL) so shaping never crosses the digits.
techniques.timing: 6-8 f after the digits
techniques.use_when: Every number that needs a unit to mean anything.
techniques.avoid_when: The unit repeats the number — pick one word.

techniques.name: A press has depth, a release has none
techniques.summary: Pressing scales the control to 0.97 and drops its shadow by 2 px; releasing returns on a straight ease with no overshoot.
techniques.how: `kit.around(ctx, cx, cy, {s}, ...)` with s = 1 - 0.03 * press; the shadow (`withShadow`, 14 px) drops to 12 px. Release uses `e_out` at the same duration — no spring, because `e_back` here reads as a bounce.
techniques.timing: press 4 f, release 6 f
techniques.use_when: Any tappable thing that is actually tapped on screen.
techniques.avoid_when: Anything that is not pressed — a bobbing card is decoration.

techniques.name: The knob travels, the colour flips
techniques.summary: A switch: the knob covers most of the track in ten frames while the track colour swaps at the midpoint.
techniques.how: Track `gray_1` to `red`, knob `paper` positioned by `e_io(p)`; at p >= 0.5 the track switches instantly (no tween) and the knob takes a 1 px ink hairline. `kit.rr` in K, `lib.rrect` in P.
techniques.timing: 10 f, flip at 5 f
techniques.use_when: On/off states the voice-over names.
techniques.avoid_when: A toggle that toggles nothing on screen afterwards.

techniques.name: The check draws itself
techniques.summary: The tick is stroked, not popped: two segments, eight to ten frames, after the row it belongs to has landed.
techniques.how: P: `checkmark(s)` gives the shape; draw it in two passes clipped by p (long stroke, then short). K: stroke a two-segment path the same way. Colour from the palette (`blush` on dark, `red` on light) — the green check is gone.
techniques.timing: 8-10 f, after the row settles
techniques.use_when: Completion, validation, done.
techniques.avoid_when: Twelve ticks at once; pick the three that matter.

techniques.name: Typing, and a caret that only blinks when idle
techniques.summary: Text types at a stated speed and the caret blinks only in the gaps; Arabic is revealed right to left as whole shaped lines.
techniques.how: K: `typeLines(ctx, lines, t, {cps})` time-boxes the reveal and clips Arabic instead of splitting letters. P: the same with `text_sprite` and a clip that grows by whole words. Caret = 3 px ink bar, 0.5 Hz blink, hidden while the character count is changing.
techniques.timing: cps 22-45, caret 1 s cycle
techniques.use_when: A prompt, a command, a message being composed.
techniques.avoid_when: Typing anything longer than about 60 characters; time-box it or cut it.
